why: Option 1 is turned a quarter turn to get options 2 and 4, and half a turn to get option 3. When the figure turns, the lines inside must turn too: vertical lines become horizontal after a quarter turn, but stay vertical after a half turn. Option 3 is a half turn of option 1, so its lines should be vertical, but they are horizontal. Option 4 may look different, but it is just option 1 turned a quarter turn the other way.
trick: When figures are rotations of each other, rotate the shading lines in your head too; a wrong line direction gives away the odd one.
note: The book key prints (8) for this question, which is impossible (only 5 figures). Most likely a misprint of 3; option 3 is the only figure that breaks the rotation rule, so book_answer/correct are set to option 3. A pen tick on the scan is on figure 4.
